diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..6b5a78f8efd71d6c2922b0e4776424d4e563a5b5 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -360,6 +360,9 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
     create a nicer looking title. :func:`titleize` is meant for creating pretty
     output.
 
+    Words written in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they are if the
+    string also contains lowercase letters.
+
     Examples::
 
       >>> titleize("man from the boondocks")
@@ -370,13 +373,46 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
 
     """
-    return re.sub(
-        r"\b('?\w)",
-        lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
-        humanize(underscore(word)).title()
-    )
+    if not any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        # There is no telling acronyms from other words in an all-caps string
+        # like "HELLO WORLD", so it is titleized as it always has been.
+        return re.sub(
+            r"\b('?\w)",
+            lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
+            humanize(underscore(word)).title()
+        )
+
+    def is_acronym(part: str) -> bool:
+        # Two or more capitals in a row, like "NASA" or "HTML5"
+        return part.isupper() and any(
+            a.isupper() and b.isupper() for a, b in zip(part, part[1:]))
+
+    def capitalize(match: typing.Match[str]) -> str:
+        apostrophe, part = match.groups()
+        # Keep acronyms, like "NASA", and words in capitals with an apostrophe,
+        # like "DON'T", but not a capital after an apostrophe in a word that
+        # isn't one, like "David'S" or "I'M".
+        if is_acronym(part) or (apostrophe and part.isupper() and is_acronym(
+                re.split(r"\W", match.string[:match.start()])[-1])):
+            return match.group()
+        part = part.capitalize()
+        if apostrophe:
+            part = part[0].lower() + part[1:]
+        return apostrophe + part
+
+    # The same as humanize(underscore(word)), except that the case is kept
+    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = word.replace("-", "_")
+    word = re.sub(r"_[iI][dD]$", "", word)
+    word = word.replace("_", " ")
+    return re.sub(r"\b('?)(\w+)", capitalize, word)

@@ -197,6 +198,16 @@ MIXTURE_TO_TITLEIZED: TestParameters = (
     ("david's Code",          "David's Code"),
     ("ana índia",             "Ana Índia"),
     ("Ana Índia",             "Ana Índia"),
+    ('NASA rocket launch',    'NASA Rocket Launch'),
+    ('read the HTTP spec',    'Read The HTTP Spec'),
+    ('NASA_rocket_launch',    'NASA Rocket Launch'),
+    ('HTMLTidy',              'HTML Tidy'),
+    ('HTML5 spec',            'HTML5 Spec'),
+    ("NASA's rocket",         "NASA's Rocket"),

+    ('HELLO WORLD',           'Hello World'),
+    ('SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE',  'Screaming Snake Case'),
 )
description: Non-acronym words are capitalized with str.capitalize() instead of the original title-casing, so acronym-free inputs with a letter after a digit change: titleize('3d model') -> '3d Model' (original '3D Model'), titleize('mp3player') -> 'Mp3player' (original 'Mp3Player').

labels.note: Derived from an own corrected implementation (reference patch plus an apostrophe fix so inputs without two consecutive capitals match base exactly); the defect is the only change relative to it.
